articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related Entities, Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations, Issues New General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations, alongside the removal of certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea. This action also included the issuance of new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses, and amendments to existing Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).

Among the Iran-related designations, OFAC added Ioanis Karnakis Kosmas, a Panamanian national, to the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List. Additionally, the entity Amigoz Singapore Pte. Ltd. and several vessels were added to the SDN List for their involvement in Iran's shadow fleet operations.

In a separate move, OFAC removed certain individuals and entities from the SDN List related to Belarus and North Korea. The agency also issued Russia-related General License 131K, authorizing specific transactions for the negotiation and entry into contingent contracts for the sale of Lukoil International GmbH and related maintenance activities.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Chinese Entities Under Protecting American Intellectual Property Act, Issues General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has implemented designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA), targeting five entities located in Beijing and Shanghai, China. These entities have been added to OFAC's Non-SDN Menu-Based Sanctions List (NS-MBS List).

The designated entities include Beijing Qiji Chuangtan Phase I Venture Capital Center Limited Partnership (a.k.a. Miracle Plus RMB Fund I), Beijing Qiji Chuangtan Phase II Venture Capital Center Limited Partnership (a.k.a. Miracle Plus RMB Fund II), Beijing Qiji Chuangtan Zhiyuan Enterprise Management Center Limited Partnership, Qiji Chuangtan Beijing Investment Management Co Ltd (a.k.a. MiraclePlus), and Shanghai Zhisuan Technology Co Ltd.

Concurrently, OFAC issued PAIPA General License 1, authorizing transactions pursuant to the Cyber-Related Sanctions Regulations, and PAIPA General License 2, which permits the wind-down of transactions involving certain entities blocked on October 19, 2026.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License for Earthquake Relief
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued Venezuela-related General License (GL) 60A, titled 'Authorizing Transactions Related to Earthquake Relief Efforts in Venezuela.' This amended general license supersedes GL 60 and extends the authorization period for earthquake relief efforts.
In conjunction with the issuance of GL 60A, OFAC also published an amended Frequently Asked Question (FAQ 1263) to provide further clarity on the scope and application of the updated authorization.

The extension of this authorization aims to facilitate ongoing humanitarian efforts and support for earthquake relief in Venezuela, allowing for continued transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under Venezuela Sanctions Regulations.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related Designations, Designates Cuban Bank, Issues New General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and a specific designation targeting a Cuban entity. These actions are part of an ongoing campaign to disrupt financial networks supporting Iran and its proxies, and to further restrict transactions with Cuba.

As part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' OFAC designated several financial institutions, companies, exchange houses, and individuals involved in Iran's financial and petroleum sectors. This includes Iraq-based International Development Bank for Investment and Finance (IDB), accused of providing financial facilitation and U.S. dollar access for Iran.

Additionally, the U.S. Department of State designated Cuba-based Banco Internacional de Comercio S.A. (BICSA) pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14404, citing its provision of services to the sanctioned Iran-based Karafarin Bank since at least 2022. OFAC also issued new and amended General Licenses and Frequently Asked Questions to guide compliance.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Venezuelan Politician Jorge Rodriguez Gomez from Sanctions List
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced the removal of Jorge Jesus Rodriguez Gomez from its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List. Rodriguez Gomez, a prominent Venezuelan politician, was previously designated under Venezuela-related sanctions.

This delisting signifies the lifting of asset freezes and the removal of obstacles for U.S. persons seeking to engage in transactions with him. Rodriguez Gomez has served as the President of Venezuela's National Assembly since 2021 and was formerly a vice president under Hugo Chavez.

His initial designation in 2018 was part of broader sanctions targeting members of Nicolas Maduro's inner circle. The removal comes amid Washington's latest push for diplomacy and an expansion of energy investment in Venezuela.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations under its Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism sanctions programs. These actions target individuals and entities involved in illicit drug trafficking and supporting terrorist activities globally.

These designations aim to disrupt the financial and logistical networks of criminal organizations and terrorist groups, preventing them from accessing the U.S. financial system and limiting their ability to operate internationally.

Further details regarding the specific individuals and entities designated, as well as the reasons for their inclusion on the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, are available in OFAC's official release.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates International Criminal Court, Issues General Licenses, and Removes Burma-Related Designation
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has designated the entire International Criminal Court (ICC) to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List) pursuant to Executive Order 14203. This action follows previous designations of individuals associated with the ICC.

Concurrently with the designation, OFAC issued four general licenses (GLs 13-16) authorizing specified transactions involving the ICC. These licenses include a 180-day wind-down authorization for operations, contracts, and agreements, as well as authorizations for telecommunications, enterprise software, pension payments, and transactions related to certain ICC detainees.

In addition to the ICC designation, OFAC announced a settlement agreement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics and removed a Burma-related designation. The EU has expressed regret over the U.S. decision to sanction the ICC and urged a reversal of the measures.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Global Sanctions and Export Controls Blog

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued a new Russia-related General License. This license authorizes specific activities that would otherwise be prohibited under existing Russia sanctions programs.
General licenses are designed to allow certain transactions to proceed without the need for individual applications, streamlining processes for U.S. persons engaging in authorized activities.
Further details regarding the scope and specific authorizations of this new Russia-related General License are available in the official OFAC publication.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related Designations, Issues New Iran and Amended Russia General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations as part of its ongoing efforts to counter Iran's illicit activities. These designations target entities and individuals supporting Iran's shadow fleet network.

In conjunction with these designations, OFAC issued a new Iran-related General License, providing specific authorizations for certain transactions. Additionally, an existing Russia-related General License has been amended to reflect updated policy or operational considerations.
These actions underscore the U.S. government's commitment to intensifying 'Operation Economic Outcast' against Iran's financial and maritime networks, while also adjusting measures related to Russia.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / U.S. Department of State

articles.headline: Bank of America Settles with OFAC for $11,662,930 Over Sanctions Violations
body: Bank of America, N.A. has agreed to pay $11,662,930 to settle its potential civil liability for 475 apparent violations of various OFAC sanctions programs. These programs include those targeting Russia, Belarus, Iran, Burma, Somalia, narcotics, and global terrorism.

The apparent violations stemmed from Bank of America processing payments involving blocked banks, failing to prioritize alerts for customers matching blocked persons, not promptly updating watchlists after OFAC designations, and mishandling business accounts associated with blocked persons due to human error.

OFAC determined that the apparent violations were non-egregious but largely not voluntarily self-disclosed. This settlement is part of a broader enforcement action by the U.S. Treasury, which also included significant penalties from FinCEN and the OCC.

The specific details of the apparent violations were outlined in OFAC's settlement agreement. These actions underscore the importance of robust compliance programs for companies operating internationally, particularly those involved in logistics and shipping.
This penalty serves as a reminder to businesses of all sizes about the potential risks and consequences of failing to adhere to OFAC regulations.

articles.headline: EU Adopts Largest-Ever Sanctions Package Against Russia's Military-Industrial Complex
body: The European Union has adopted its 22nd package of sanctions against Russia, marking the largest single expansion of its sanctions list since 2022. This package adds 1,569 individuals and entities to the EU sanctions lists, bringing the total number of designations under the Ukraine-related sanctions regime to almost 4,600.

The new measures primarily target Russia's military-industrial complex, including 826 Russian companies and 743 individuals. These entities are involved in the production and supply of components used in missiles, drones, military aircraft, and related defense technologies.

The EU's action responds to Russia's continued aggression against Ukraine and recent attacks on civilian infrastructure. The package emphasizes additional designations and asset freezes, with a focus on disrupting the financial, logistical, and commercial networks supporting Russia's war effort.

articles.headline: US Proposes Restrictions on Investments in Sensitive Iranian Technology Sectors
body: The U.S. Treasury Department has proposed new rules that would restrict American investments in sensitive technology sectors within Iran and four other countries deemed national security concerns. These rules aim to curb the flow of U.S. capital and expertise to these nations.

Under the proposed regulations, U.S. firms and individuals would be required to notify the Treasury about certain prospective investments in Iran, China, Cuba, North Korea, and Russia. Some transactions would be outright prohibited.

This initiative is part of a broader strategy to financially isolate Iran, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent having launched 'Operation Economic Outcast' earlier this year, calling for the closure of all Bank Melli branches abroad.

articles.headline: OCC Announces Enforcement Actions for October 2026, Including Penalties Against American Express and Bank of America
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) has released its enforcement actions for October 2026, highlighting significant penalties against American Express National Bank and Bank of America, National Association. These actions address deficiencies in their Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) compliance programs.

American Express National Bank received a Cease and Desist Order and a $350 million civil money penalty for failures in its BSA compliance, untimely suspicious activity reports, and violations related to customer due diligence and identification programs.

Bank of America, National Association, was assessed a $750 million civil money penalty for similar BSA compliance program deficiencies, failure to timely file suspicious activity reports, and sending wires with inaccurate transmittor name information. The OCC also issued Orders of Prohibition against two individuals for embezzlement.

body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) published: "Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports". Full details are available on federalregister.gov.

articles.headline: Revisions to the Entity List
body: In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) revises the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by removing two addresses associated with Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. from the Entity List under the destination of China, People's Republic of (China). This determination follows the removal from the Entity List of Arrow China Electronics Trading Co., Ltd., and the removal of six aliases for Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. in November 2025.

articles.headline: Removal From the Entity List
body: In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by removing one entity from the Entity List under the destination of Turkey.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
